issue.title: Fail to build v1.4.0 or later on armv7
issue.body:
Since version 1.4.0 (v1.3.1 and before is ok), I can not build my code on a Raspberry Pi 3b+ with the following issue:

```
/usr/include/mavsdk/plugins/mavlink_passthrough/mavlink_include.h:3:10: fatal error: mavlink/v2.0/common/mavlink.h: No such file or directory
#include "mavlink/v2.0/common/mavlink.h"
```

I will dig into the modifications but I just open an issue if @julianoes or @JonasVautherin you already see what it could be. I will try with a simple MAVSDK example to see if the issue remains

comments.body: Just to be sure: did you try a clean build? There were some changes in mavlink as a third party library, so you may have to rebuild the third parties as well (i.e. clean build the whole project).
I use MAVSDK in a docker by getting the `.deb` package so it should be as clean as possible yes. I'm building from zero on a RPi but it takes hours :) I let you know once it's built and tested

And do you set `-DMAVLINK_HEADERS`, like [in the CI](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/.github/workflows/main.yml#L308)? This is fairly new, and it should work with the default, but worth having a look :+1:.

I do something like this in my Dockerfile:

```
RUN wget https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/releases/download/v${MAVSDK_VERSION}/libmavsdk-dev_${MAVSDK_VERSION}_${MAVSDK_PKG}.deb \
&& sudo dpkg -i libmavsdk-dev_${MAVSDK_VERSION}_${MAVSDK_PKG}.deb \
```

But you mean I need to add it if I build from source ? Looks like this flag has been added [two months ago](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/commit/890deef6556baf28a34363b12be6571fd46234e2) so it is already in v1.3.1 as well as v1.4.0 so the debian package should have this modification right ?
Oh, sorry, I misunderstood. So you install the package, but then it fails building your code. :thinking:

exactly yes :) 

Would it be possible that there are extra quotes on the debian install [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/e619fbbdfee674a346d8ce1de70d99426c59d7c9/debian/rules#L15) ? I don't see them in the in the CI or it does not change the build command ?
Not sure :confused:. Did you try installing a package on your laptop and e.g. compiling the examples? Would be faster to debug than doing everything on the RPi :grin:

I had to do some more modifications to this mavlink header inclusion in this PR: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1768

It would be good to have a way to reproduce this locally in docker.
Installing the pacakge ubuntu20.04_amd64 on a linux host works fine. To test locally would it work if I build the package for armv7 and use it in my dockerfile instead of the v1.4.3 ?

I just built a debian package for armv7 with main branch but I still have the issue. I tried the PR you mentioned @julianoes and  it looks like my issue is gone, but I guess there are a lot of changes and I need to adapt my code...

```
mavsdk::MavlinkPassthrough' {aka 'class mavsdk::MavlinkPassthrough'} has no member named 'subscribe_message_async'; did you mean 'subscribe_message'?
_mavlink_passthrough->subscribe_message_async
```

I will dig into your modifications to see if I can only get the corrections of the mavlink header issue and add it on top of v1.4.3

The proper installation of mavlink header in the CMakelists in this [commit](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/commit/0c8e2367952b3233669739d439a13f2ccb568470) fixes my issue. 

Thank you ! I will work with locally build deb package until there is a new release including this modification.

@Katawann I made a pull request with that commit you mentioned: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1819

Would you mind reviewing? Let me know if that fixes your problem, so that I can merge it :+1:

rename.to: Fail to build v1.4.0 or later on armv7
